cards.explanation: The answer is: Take your positions and prepare yourself. The call goes out loud to Migdol, Memphis and Tahpanhes: “Take your positions and prepare yourself, for the sword devours those around you.” (Jeremiah 46:14) It's a get-ready message, friends. So it's about getting into position, not sitting still.

The answer is the LORD. The text says the warriors cannot stand, “…for the LORD has thrust them down.” (Jeremiah 46:15) So this isn't a clumsy day or a slippery floor, friends. It's the LORD's doing, and that changes how you read the whole scene.

The answer is True! The warriors say, “Get up! Let us return to our people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor.” (Jeremiah 46:16) That's a whole group saying they want out of there. So going back to their own people and the land of their birth is exactly what the text has them say.

The answer is that he was all noise and let his time pass. The warriors cry out, “Pharaoh king of Egypt was all noise; he has let the appointed time pass him by.” (Jeremiah 46:17) That's a lot of volume and not much follow-through, friends. I know that feeling. I once stamped a whole tray of cookies and forgot to turn the oven on.

The answer is True. The King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, says, “As surely as I live…” (Jeremiah 46:18) That's a promise sworn on His own life. When He says one is coming, you can count on it, friends.

The answer is exile. The LORD says, “Pack your bags for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt!” (Jeremiah 46:19) Memphis will be laid waste, destroyed and uninhabited, so staying put isn't the plan. It's a heavy line, friends.

The answer is a gadfly! The LORD says, “Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north is coming against her.” (Jeremiah 46:20) A gadfly is a pesky fly, and the picture is a beautiful animal being pestered by something small. Anybody who's tried to swat one knows it's no small trouble.

The answer is False. The text says the mercenaries “…will turn back; together they will flee, they will not stand their ground, for the day of calamity is coming upon them…” (Jeremiah 46:21) They're called like fattened calves, and no one is holding the line. Everybody heads for the exit together, friends.

The answer is serpent! The text says, “Egypt will hiss like a fleeing serpent, for the enemy will advance in force…” (Jeremiah 46:22) That's the sound of something slithering off in a hurry, friends. The enemy advancing in force is what sets it off.

The answer is that they are more numerous than locusts. The LORD says they will chop down her forest, “…dense though it may be, for they are more numerous than locusts; they cannot be counted.” (Jeremiah 46:23) So it isn't about the trees being weak, friends. It's about how many are coming.

The answer is True. The text says, “The Daughter of Egypt will be put to shame; she will be delivered into the hands of the people of the north.” (Jeremiah 46:24) Both things are said together in that one verse, friends. It's a heavy line.

The answer is Thebes. The LORD says, “Behold, I am about to punish Amon god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, Egypt with her gods and kings, and those who trust in Pharaoh.” (Jeremiah 46:25) So Amon is named right there with Egypt's gods. It's a long list, friends.

The answer is that it will be inhabited as in days of old. The LORD says, “But after this, Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 46:26) After the hard part, people live there again, friends. That little word “after” does a lot of work in this verse.

The answer is: Do not be afraid. The LORD says, “But you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel.” (Jeremiah 46:27) After all that noise about Egypt, here comes a gentle turn, friends. The text puts Jacob and Israel side by side.

The answer is ease! The text says, “Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.” (Jeremiah 46:27) Quiet and ease, and nobody around to scare him, friends. That sounds like the best porch in the world.

The answer is that the LORD is with him. The LORD says, “And you, My servant Jacob, do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you.” (Jeremiah 46:28) It isn't a plan or a map, friends. The reason is that He is with Jacob.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Yet I will discipline you justly, and will by no means leave you unpunished.” (Jeremiah 46:28) He won't completely destroy Jacob, and He also won't skip the discipline. Both are in the same verse, friends, and I think that's worth sitting with.
